raw_segments.text: He wore a long, unsleeved garment of recently-flayed oxide reaching to the knees in a loose kilt,
and this was bound about his middle by a girdle of plated straw and rushes.
Beneath this, he wore trues of deerskin, roughly stitched with gut.
His nether extremities were encased in high Balbriggan buskins dyed in lichen purple,
the feet being shod with brogues of salted cowhide laced with the windpipe of the same
beast.
From his girdle hung a row of sea stones which jangled at every movement of his portentous
frame, and on these were graven with rude yet striking art the tribal images of many
Irish heroes and heroines of antiquity.
Cuchulain, Khan of Hundred Battles, Nile of Nine Hostages, Brian of Kincora, the
Ardry Malachi, Art Mack Murrog, Shane O'Neill, Father John Murphy, Owen Rowe, Patrick Sarsfield,
Red Hugh O'Donnell, Red Jim Mack Dermot, Sagarth Iagan O'Groney, Michael Dwyer,
Francie Higgins, Henry Joy M. Kraken, Goliath, Horace Wheatley, Thomas Knapp, Peg Woffington,
The Village Blacksmith, Captain Moonlight, Captain Boycott, Dante Oligary, Christopher
Columbus, S. Versa, S. Brendan, Marshall Macman, Charlemagne, Theobald Wolf Tone, The Mother
of the Maccabees, The Last of the Mohicans, The Rose of Castille, The Man for Galway,
The Man That Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo, The Man in the Gap, The Woman Who Didn't,
Benjamin Franklin, Napoleon Bonaparte, John L. Sullivan, Cleopatra.
Saverneen Delish, Julius Caesar, Paracelsus, Sir Thomas Lipton, William Tell, Michelangelo
Hayes, Mohammed, The Bride of Lamermore, Peter the Hermit, Peter the Packer, Dark Rosaline,
Patrick W. Shakespeare, Brian Confucius, Murdoch Gutenberg, Patricio Velasquez, Captain Nemo,
Tristan and Isolde, The First Prince of Wales, Thomas Cook and Son, The Bold Soldier Boy,
Arana Pogg, Dick Turpin, Ludwig Beethoven, The Colleen Bonn, Wadler Healy, Angus the
Bride, Ben Howth, Valentine Greatrakes, Adam and Eve, Arthur Wellesley, Boss Kroker, Herodotus,
Jack the Giant Hiller, Gautama Buddha, Lady Godiva, The Lily of Killarney, Balor of the
Evil Eye, The Queen of Sheba, Aki Nagel, Joe Nagel, Alessandro Volta, Jeremiah O'Donovan-Rasa,
Don Philip O'Sullivan Bear. A couched spear of a cuminated granite rested by him, while
at his feet reposed a savage animal of the canine tribe, whose sturderest gasps announced
that he was sunk in uneasy slumber, a supposition confirmed by horse growls and spasmodic movements,
which his master repressed from time to time by tranquilizing blows of a mighty cudgel
rudely fashioned out of paleolithic stone.
